about: The ideas board. Every idea or suggestion goes through the loop in .github/IDEAS.md (propose, challenge, score, John approves, test, measure, learn) before it reaches the site. Targets are directions only: real numbers stay in John's private email. kind "duty" = an always-on responsibility (doesn't change what visitors see, so it doesn't count towards the limit of 3 tests at once); kind "test" = a change visitors see, tested and measured.

ideas.title: Ads and consumer-law check on every page and post
ideas.problem: We earn commission from links, and social posts promote deals. UK advertising rules (ASA/CAP) and consumer law (CMA, the DMCC Act) apply to affiliate content. One complaint could cost us a retailer programme.
ideas.evidence: These rules apply to affiliate marketing in the UK. The editor already checks for fake urgency and "was" prices; there's no check yet for disclosure on every page with buy links, or for social captions that promote affiliate deals.
ideas.hypothesis: If the editor checks for a clear affiliate disclosure on every page with buy links and for correct labelling in social captions, against the current ASA/CAP guidance, then the risk of a complaint or a lost programme drops to near zero, at almost no cost.
ideas.test: Add the checks to agent_editor.py, run them over the whole site once and fix what fails in one Fix pack.
ideas.metric: pages and posts failing the check
ideas.risks: Over-labelling could make the site feel salesy: keep the wording short and friendly. The guidance must be read from the ASA/CMA's own pages, not from memory.
ideas.challenge: Objective: trust (it protects revenue). Evidence: the rules are public. Smallest test: one run and one Fix pack. Backfire: only if the wording is clumsy. Duplicate: no. Cost: none. Undo: remove the check.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude at John's request.

John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the editor holds any page with buy links but no commission disclosure, and --audit sweeps the whole site (first sweep: every page with buy links already discloses).

ideas.title: Retailer programme health watch
ideas.owner: the revenue guardian (with the coverage hunter)
ideas.problem: A retailer's affiliate programme can pause, close, change its commission or break its deep links without warning, and the money stops quietly.
ideas.evidence: The revenue guardian already checks links land on the right shop and reads private Awin figures, so the data is there; nothing yet watches each programme's status, or applications still pending.
ideas.hypothesis: If the revenue guardian flags within a day any programme that pauses, closes, changes terms or stops recording clicks, and the coverage hunter chases pending applications, then fewer buy clicks go unpaid.
ideas.test: Add a programme-status table to the private revenue email, with an alert when a programme changes or clicks stop being recorded for 48 hours.
ideas.metric: buy clicks that go to a programme that isn't paying
ideas.target: down to zero within a day of any change
ideas.risks: Must never change which price is shown first because of commission: the cheapest honest price always leads. Private figures stay private.
ideas.challenge: Objective: revenue. Evidence: our own Awin data. Smallest test: an email table. Backfire: none on the site. Duplicate: extends the revenue guardian. Cost: free. Undo: remove the table.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.
John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the revenue guardian checks daily for programmes no longer joined and for retailers whose clicks stopped being recorded, and emails John the same day.

ideas.title: New-model launch season: "last year's model, now cheaper" pages
ideas.owner: the seasonal planner (with the catalogue autopilot and the moments planner)
ideas.problem: Golf's big equipment launches come each new year, and last season's models tend to drop in price. That's exactly what GolfPrice AI is for, yet the seasonal planner has no occasion for it.
ideas.evidence: Industry pattern (benchmark, not yet our own data); our price history will confirm or deny it model by model. Pages are built 8 weeks ahead, so the window to prepare is now.
ideas.hypothesis: If we add a launch-season occasion (new models added fast; last year's models with their price movement shown honestly from our own history), then search visits and buy clicks rise in January to March.
ideas.test: One occasion page plus the catalogue adding new models within a day of launch; social posts planned by the moments planner.
ideas.metric: visits and buy clicks on the occasion page and the previous-model price pages, against the weeks before
ideas.risks: Only show price falls our own data proves (no "was" prices, no implied saving we can't show). Never name retailers. Launch dates must be verified.
ideas.challenge: Objective: traffic and revenue. Evidence: benchmark, confidence 3. Smallest test: one page. Backfire: claims that aren't proven, so the claims guardian checks it. Duplicate: no. Cost: free. Undo: unpublish the page.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude. Time-sensitive: needs approving by mid-December.

John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: a "Club launch season" occasion page (clubs and balls at the lowest price we have tracked), refreshed weekly from 25 Nov; the moments planner and newsroom can point posts at it.

ideas.title: The analyst measures every test, and spots sudden drops
ideas.problem: Without a before-and-after for each idea, we can't tell what worked; and a sudden drop (a broken page, a lost ranking, a dead link) can go unnoticed until the weekly review.
ideas.evidence: The analyst already has the private counts and the button test; it doesn't yet read the ideas board or alert on sudden drops.
ideas.hypothesis: If the analyst reads every "testing" idea in data/ideas.json and reports its metric against the period before, and emails John within a day when visits or buy clicks fall sharply, then decisions get faster and problems shorter.
ideas.test: Add both to agent_performance.py and the private email.
ideas.metric: ideas with a measured result; time from a sudden drop to John hearing of it
ideas.target: every test measured; under a day
ideas.risks: False alarms from normal weekly swings: compare like-for-like days and set a sensible threshold.
ideas.challenge: Needed for the loop to work at all. Evidence: our own data. Cost: free. Undo: remove it.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.

John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the analyst measures every testing idea (before vs since; directions public, numbers private), emails a sudden-drop alert the same day, and lists the top pages (order only) for the shopper.

ideas.title: Free-tier and budget guard
ideas.problem: We rely on free tiers (Cloudflare Workers and D1, Brevo's daily sends, GitHub Actions) and an approved OpenMontage budget of USD 10 every two weeks. Going over a limit can stop emails or the worker without warning.
ideas.evidence: The Cloudflare Observability email showed how easy it is to be surprised; Brevo's free plan has a daily cap.
ideas.hypothesis: If the watchdog checks usage against each limit and warns John at 80%, then nothing stops unexpectedly and nothing is charged.
ideas.test: Add the usage checks the free APIs allow to agent_watchdog.py; where there's no API, count our own sends and requests.
ideas.metric: surprises (a stopped service or a charge)
ideas.challenge: Objective: efficiency and trust. Evidence: our own setup. Cost: free. Undo: remove it.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.
John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the watchdog warns at 80% of Brevo's daily emails and (with an optional Cloudflare token) Worker and D1 limits, and flags a private repo.

ideas.title: The search-to-page engine drafts the top search gaps as pages
ideas.owner: the search-to-page engine (with the competitor watch)
ideas.problem: The SEO and competitor reports find searches we have no page for, but only list them.
ideas.evidence: seo-opportunities and competitor-watch "gaps" (our data plus competitors). Comparison searches such as "model A vs model B price" suit a price site.
ideas.hypothesis: If the engine drafts the top 3 gaps each month as genuinely useful pages (real prices from our data, honest comparison), then search visits rise on those queries.
ideas.test: 3 draft pages on a branch for John; each passes the editor; measure their search visits after 6 weeks.
ideas.metric: search visits to the new pages
ideas.target: each page earning visits within 6 weeks
ideas.risks: Thin or near-duplicate pages count against us with Google: only build where we have real, distinct value; no doorway pages.
ideas.challenge: Objective: traffic. Evidence: our own gap data, confidence 3. Smallest test: 3 pages. Backfire: thin content, so the editor checks usefulness. Undo: noindex or remove.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.
John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the monthly AI and competitor check drafts the top 3 search gaps as pages on a branch each month.

ideas.title: Price-alert sign-up at the moment of interest
ideas.problem: Visitors who aren't ready to buy leave with no way back. Price alerts bring them back when the price falls, which is when they buy.
ideas.evidence: Price alerts and the weekly digest already exist; the sign-up prompt's placement hasn't been tested.
ideas.hypothesis: If we test one extra, polite sign-up prompt at the moment of interest (after a game result, or when a visitor leaves a price page without clicking), then sign-ups rise without hurting buy clicks.
ideas.test: One split test on price pages through the analyst's button test.
ideas.metric: sign-ups per visit, with buy clicks as a guardrail
ideas.target: sign-ups up, buy clicks not down
ideas.risks: Pop-ups annoy people: no pop-up that blocks the page, easy to dismiss, shown once.
ideas.challenge: Objective: retention. Evidence: hunch to benchmark. Smallest test: one split test. Guardrail: buy clicks. Undo: switch off.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.
John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: a polite, dismissible "Not buying today?" bar, split-tested by the analyst (sign-ups up, buy clicks as the guardrail); it starts through the Fix pack.

ideas.title: Quick-answer lines for the questions golfers ask AI apps
ideas.problem: AI apps quote pages that answer a question directly; ours often bury the answer.
ideas.evidence: The monthly AI-answer check measures which of 10 questions we're found for.
ideas.hypothesis: If the most relevant page for each missing question opens with a one-sentence, visible answer, then we're found for more of them.
ideas.test: Add quick answers to the pages for the 3 biggest gaps.
ideas.metric: AI-style questions we're found for (out of 10)
ideas.risks: Must be written for people and visible on the page (nothing aimed only at AI crawlers).
ideas.challenge: Evidence: our own monthly check, confidence 3. Cheap. Undo: remove the lines.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.
John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the monthly AI and competitor check writes visible quick-answer lines for the 3 biggest AI-answer gaps on a branch.

ideas.title: Monthly mobile check of the top landing pages
ideas.problem: Most visitors are on phones; a slow or awkward first screen loses buy clicks.
ideas.evidence: The mystery shopper already walks the site; seo-health flags slow pages.
ideas.hypothesis: If the shopper checks the 10 most-visited landing pages on a phone each month (speed, the price and buy button above the fold, nothing covering them), fixing what fails raises buy clicks.
ideas.test: One audit and one Fix pack.
ideas.metric: buy clicks per visit on the fixed pages
ideas.challenge: Evidence: benchmark, confidence 3. Cheap. Undo: revert the fix.

history.note: Proposed and challenged by Claude.

John approved all nine shortlisted ideas. Built: the mystery shopper checks the 10 most-visited price pages on a phone every night (price and buy button on the first screen, nothing covering it, big enough to tap, under 3.5 seconds).

ideas.title: Society HQ as a word-of-mouth engine
ideas.owner: the society connector (with the game master)
ideas.problem: Each society organiser can bring a whole group; we don't know how many invites turn into new visitors.
ideas.evidence: Hunch so far: no invite data yet.
ideas.hypothesis: If organisers get a one-tap invite and share card, each society brings several new regulars.
ideas.test: First count invites and the visitors they bring for 4 weeks; then decide.
ideas.risks: No spam: invites are sent by the organiser, never by us.
ideas.challenge: Confidence too low to build yet. Bring back when the analyst has 4 weeks of invite data.

history.note: Needs invite data first (the analyst can count it).

ideas.title: Press desk: golf clubs, societies, podcasts and YouTubers
ideas.problem: Links and mentions from golf media and clubs bring visitors and help rankings.
ideas.evidence: Hunch to benchmark; the press desk already pitches writers.
ideas.hypothesis: If the press desk offers free, genuinely useful things (Society HQ for club newsletters, a monthly price-trend stat for podcasts), we earn mentions and links.
ideas.test: Pitch 5 club or society newsletters with Society HQ; count replies and mentions.
ideas.risks: Never pay for links (against Google's rules); respect opt-outs.
ideas.challenge: Low confidence and some effort; a cheap 5-pitch test would raise confidence.

history.note: Run the 5-pitch test when the press desk has capacity.

ideas.title: Repurpose the best Reel to YouTube Shorts and Pinterest
ideas.problem: Each video is made once and posted mostly to Instagram.
ideas.evidence: Hunch: Pinterest suits gift guides, but we have no account data.
ideas.hypothesis: Reposting the week's best Reel widens reach at no extra cost.
ideas.test: Post manually for 4 weeks before automating.
ideas.risks: Needs new accounts and John's time.
ideas.challenge: Costs John's time and needs accounts; park until Instagram is running smoothly.

history.note: Revisit once Instagram posting is settled.

wipNote: Tests start one page area at a time: launch season and the alert nudge first; quick answers and gap pages start as their monthly branches are merged, keeping at most 3 tests running.
